rationale: Kremlin usually sends State Duma Speaker Volodin or Foreign Minister Lavrov to top Iranian funerals (Volodin at Raisi 2024; Lavrov also attended), while Putin rarely goes; no Kremlin announcement yet as of June 24.

Syria's security bureaucracy is run by al-Sharaa loyalists; Salama is GIS director and National Security Council member, former GIS chief Anas Khattab is now Interior Minister (unlikely to move), and no National Security Bureau appointment has been signalled since Assad's bureau was dissolved in 2025.

Multiple reports (RBC-Ukraine, TASS, June media) say Zelensky intends to replace Syrskii with Budanov (now presidential office chief) in a reshuffle, with Fedorov also floating Biletskyi; Syrskii remains in post but under strain as Konstantinivka falls.

Iran-aligned Iraqi militias (Kataib Hezbollah, AAH, Nujaba) have repeatedly attacked US personnel and Iran set up cells in Iraq for attacks on Gulf states; the fragile MoU makes further US retaliation in Iraq plausible, and Houthis resumed attacks in June despite ceasefire nuances.

Houthis re-banned Israeli shipping June 8 and attacks could resume; existing Prosperity Guardian and Aspides exist so a 'new' coalition would likely be Gulf-led by Saudi Arabia (or an expanded US effort), with no announcement yet as of June 24.

Five candidates nominated with first straw polls expected late July/August; Grossi, the IAEA chief, is the highest-profile with US/Western traction, followed by Grynspan and Bachelet, but Latin American fragmentation and P5 dynamics add uncertainty.

Suu Kyi was moved to house arrest in late April; the Philippines (ASEAN chair) and Western embassies have explicitly demanded access for the ASEAN special envoy and UN representatives, making ASEAN the most likely first visitor, though nothing confirmed yet.

Ye Win Oo (C-in-C since March 30) has had only inbound engagements (Indian Navy chief visit, ASEAN video meeting) and did not join Min Aung Hlaing's China trip; India is his most active defense partner, with China/Russia credible, and no outbound visit confirmed as of June 24.

US-backed talks between Jorge Rodriguez and Dinorah Figuera began June 18-19 focused on a credible National Electoral Council and judiciary/TSJ, but the negotiating round has not yet concluded an overhaul agreement, so evidence is moderate.

Gulf states suffered heavy Iranian missile/drone attacks and UAE was hit ~2,800 times; the GCC sent a joint IMO letter against Iran's Hormuz authority, but the fragile US-Iran MoU and reconstruction-fund diplomacy make an indefinite embargo uncertain, with Saudi or UAE most likely.

Opposition politicians Tymoshenko and Poroshenko are the most likely to break the wartime-election taboo as US pressure grows; Zelensky's camp discusses elections but ties them to ceasefire/security guarantees, which may not qualify.

Treasury has run a series of 'Economic Fury' designations against Iran-aligned Iraqi militias (KH, AAH, Nujaba, KSS) in April-May 2026, suggesting continued monthly actions in August; Houthis are the biggest Iran-aligned actor but already FTO-designated.

Kremlin aide Ushakov said June 14 that Witkoff and Kushner would visit Moscow again 'in the near future' after finishing Iran work, and Peskov on June 24 said contacts will resume when they become available.

SCO summit is Aug 31-Sep 1 in Bishkek (Kyrgyzstan); Russia has pushed for India/bilateral formats, with Xi and host Japarov also plausible counterparts on Ukraine, though no specific meeting announced yet.

US has pushed Miami/Washington and rejected Russia's Switzerland/Turkey alternatives, but on June 15-17 Zelensky named the United States as a possible venue for talks with Putin in a 'neutral country' before winter; Abu Dhabi hosted earlier rounds, and no new venue has been formally announced as of June 24.
